Massive total addressable market: 700K+ active licensed restaurants in the US (per Scrap.io and commercial vendor databases), spanning full-service restaurants, limited-service/QSR, cafeterias, caterers, food trucks, and bars with food service. Comprehensive public data availability across all 50 states: Florida DBPR provides downloadable CSV files with descriptive column headers including mailing address and facility address for all active public food service establishments; Texas DSHS maintains interactive jurisdictional map and open records access for retail food establishments; New York State DOH publishes monthly-updated food service establishment inspection database via health.data.ny.gov covering 2005-present; Boston Analyze Boston portal provides downloadable active food establishment license dataset; Georgia DPH maintains food service establishment records. All restaurant licensing data is 100% public under state health and safety regulations, freedom of information laws, and FDA Model Food Code adoption — health department permits and food establishment licenses are public safety records with zero privacy restrictions. Engineering lift is moderate: scrape or download from 50+ state/county health departments (format varies — some states offer bulk CSV downloads like Florida, others require web scraping or public records requests), normalize license types (full-service restaurant, limited-service, mobile food unit, caterer, temporary food establishment), deduplicate multi-location chains while preserving individual location records, geocode addresses for location filtering, and flag inactive/suspended/closed establishments. No affordable flat-file competitor exists below $1,000 on Gumroad or similar marketplaces — all existing vendors sell either expensive subscription models ($5,000-$15,000/year enterprise subscriptions) or per-contact pricing ($0.10-0.30 which scales to $70,000-$210,000 for full 700K database, or minimum orders of $100-300), creating massive wedge opportunity for one-time $149 CSV purchase that undercuts subscriptions by 97%+ while serving the exact same B2B buyer segments. Score is 8 due to very strong validated commercial pricing ($0.10-0.30/contact baseline, multiple vendors at $100-300 minimum, 700K+ TAM confirmed), excellent public data availability with some states offering direct CSV downloads, absence of low-cost flat-file alternatives creating 27×-67× cost advantage vs. POS vendor marketing budgets, massive recurring-revenue B2B buyer base (POS systems, distributors, equipment vendors, SaaS platforms all with high customer LTV justifying database acquisition), and 700K+ addressable market representing substantial scale for niche packaging.

data_wanted: All 50 states plus DC maintain public food establishment license registries under state health and safety regulations, accessible via state and county health departments with zero authentication requirements. Florida DBPR (Department of Business and Professional Regulation) at myfloridalicense.com provides bulk downloadable CSV files with descriptive column headers covering all active public food service establishments including mailing address and facility address, organized by county and licensing district — Florida explicitly offers data extraction for public download. Texas DSHS (Department of State Health Services) at dshs.texas.gov/retail-food-establishments maintains interactive jurisdictional map of all retail food establishments enabling visitors to view information by geographic location, plus open records request process for bulk data extraction. New York State DOH publishes Food Service Establishment Inspection Data via health.data.ny.gov covering inspection information for active facilities from 2005-present, updated monthly and available for bulk download. Boston Analyze Boston open data portal (data.boston.gov) provides downloadable dataset containing active food establishment licenses. Georgia Department of Public Health maintains food service establishment records. Additional major jurisdictions: California CDPH, Illinois IDPH, Pennsylvania DOH, Ohio ODH, North Carolina DHHS, Michigan MDHHS, New Jersey DOH, Virginia VDH, Washington State DOH, Arizona ADHS, Massachusetts DPH, Tennessee TDH, Indiana ISDH, Missouri DHSS, Maryland MDH, Wisconsin DHS, Colorado CDPHE, Minnesota MDH, South Carolina DHEC, Alabama ADPH, Louisiana LDH, Kentucky CHFS, Oregon OHA, Oklahoma OSDH, Connecticut DPH, Utah UDOH, Iowa IDPH, Mississippi MSDH, Arkansas ADH, Kansas KDHE, Nevada DHHS, New Mexico DOH, West Virginia DHHR, Nebraska DHHS, Idaho DHW, Hawaii DOH, New Hampshire DHHS, Maine CDC, Montana DPHHS, Rhode Island RIDOH, Delaware DPH, South Dakota DOH, North Dakota NDDoH, Alaska DHSS, Vermont Health Department, Wyoming WDH, and Washington DC DOH. Key fields per establishment: Business name (DBA — "doing business as" trade name), owner name or operator name (individual or corporate entity where disclosed), business mailing address (for correspondence), physical facility address (street address where food service occurs), license or permit number (alphanumeric identifier unique per jurisdiction), license type or establishment classification (full-service restaurant with table service, limited-service restaurant or quick-service, mobile food dispensing vehicle or food truck, caterer or commissary, temporary food establishment for events/fairs, bar or tavern with food service, institutional food service for schools/hospitals, retail food establishment for grocery prepared foods — nomenclature varies by state but maps to FDA Food Code categories), license status (active, inactive, expired, suspended for health violations, revoked, closed/out of business), initial license or permit issue date, current expiration or renewal date (most jurisdictions require annual renewal), seating capacity (number of seats where reported), cuisine type or food service category (where classified by jurisdiction), health inspection score or letter grade (where publicly disclosed — some states publish inspection results, others restrict to pass/fail or only violations), most recent inspection date, critical violations (foodborne illness risk factors), non-critical violations, risk category (high/medium/low based on food handling complexity and volume), square footage (where reported), number of employees (where reported for larger jurisdictions), and ownership structure (sole proprietor, partnership, corporation, LLC). Target all active establishments, optionally include recently closed/inactive for prospecting (equipment liquidation, lease takeovers, re-opening consultation services). Approximately 700,000+ total licensed food establishments nationwide as of 2026: 380,000+ full-service restaurants, 240,000+ limited-service/QSR, 50,000+ mobile food units, 30,000+ caterers. Target output: 700K rows minimum, one row per licensed location (chain restaurants with multiple locations appear as separate entries per physical address). Data is 100% public per state health and safety codes, freedom of information laws, and FDA Model Food Code — food establishment permits are public safety records with no privacy restrictions under public health transparency statutes.
